en: As for the first shape of the system, we can form for ourselves only an insufficient representation of it from a few sibylline fragments that it has left behind.

The most probable thing is that Hegel did not carry any of these attempts fully through to the end, because in the course of the work the inadequacy of the form of representation to that of pure thinking became too great.
Yet there still remains a significant fragment, which deals with the divine triangle.
This geometrizing way of representing things was at that time again brought into currency by Franz Baader in his writing On the Pythagorean Square or the Four Quarters of the World, Tübingen 1798.
The philosopher of the romantic school, Jakob Böhme, too, had again come into honour with his ternary.
In his culture Hegel also passed through this form.

But since he wanted to penetrate it with scientific seriousness, and not merely to delight himself in it with mystical trifling, he had to ruin it precisely in its geometrical determinacy, as precisely in that which was supposed to be the most peculiar thing in it.
Accordingly, nothing remained but the concept of the unity that distinguishes itself threefold from itself.
Hegel's dialectical spirit was not content with a simple triangle.

In order to express the life of the idea he constructed a triangle of triangles, which he let move through one another in such a way that each not only in general became once an extreme and once a middle, but also had to undergo this process within itself with each of its sides.
But in order, in this hardness and crudeness of intuition, to keep once again also the ideal softness of the unity, the
zh: 至于体系的第一个形态，我们只能凭它留下的一些西比拉式的残片，对它形成一种不充分的表象。
最可能的是，黑格尔没有把其中任何一次尝试完全进行到底，因为在工作过程中，表象的形式与纯粹思维的形式之间的不相称变得太大了。
不过还留有一份重要的残篇，它讲的是神性三角形。
这种几何化的表象方式，当时又由弗朗茨·巴德尔在他的著作《论毕达哥拉斯正方形或四个世界方位》（图宾根，1798年）中重新带动起来。
就连浪漫派的哲学家雅各布·伯麦，也凭他的三元式重新得到了尊崇。
黑格尔在他的教养中也穿过了这种形式。
但是，既然他想以科学的严肃态度穿透它，而不只是想带着神秘的把戏在它那里自娱，他就必然恰恰在它的几何规定性上，也就是恰恰在它里面本该最独特的东西上，把它毁掉。
所以，剩下的就只有那个三重地与自己相区别的统一性的概念。
黑格尔的辩证精神并不满足于一个简单的三角形。
为了表达观念的生命，他建构了一个三角形的三角形，并让它们以这样的方式彼此穿行运动：每一个不只是一般地一度成为端项、一度成为中项，而且它还必须在自己内部就自己的每一条边都经历这一过程。
但是，为了在这种直观的坚硬和粗陋中，也重新保住统一性的观念的柔和，那

en: In order to keep the fluidity of the differences represented as triangle and sides, he went on consistently to the further barbarism of expressing the totality as a quadrilateral resting above the triangles and their process.
But in the course of the work he seems to have grown tired; at least it breaks off at the construction of the animal.
The interesting thing about this fragment consists chiefly in the energetic conflict of the woodenness of the form with the livingness of the dialectic of the content.
It had to prove to Hegel the impossibility of presenting the true in any other than a logical determinacy for cognition without violence and wild half-fantasy.
zh: 为了保持那作为三角形和边而被表象的差别的流动性，他就一贯地进而走到更进一步的野蛮做法上，即把总体性表达为一个高悬在那些三角形及其过程之上的四边形。
但在工作过程中，他好像疲倦了；至少它是在建构动物时中断的。
这份残篇的有趣之处，主要在于形式的僵硬与内容的辩证法的生动性之间那种有力的冲突。
这必然向黑格尔证明了一件事是不可能的：在逻辑规定性之外的另一种规定性中，不施暴力、不靠粗野的半幻想地为认识展示真的东西。

en: In this respect this work was for Hegel perhaps the most terrible and at the same time the most fruitful exertion.
Through his works in Bern he had struggled through from the bitterest indignation against the manifold distortions of Christianity back to trust in it and in its fundamental representations.
He now wanted to comprehend the Trinity in the triangle of triangles.
He now did not want to reject from himself as unreasonable that representation in which faith had for centuries revered its highest possession.
Becoming acquainted with the German mystics of the Middle Ages and their profound language heightened this tendency.
Already at the end of the Swiss period there are found among Hegel's papers excerpts of passages from Meister Eckart and Tauler, which he copied out for himself from literary gazettes.
But as he engaged with Gnosis, the concept of spirit pressed upon him as the one which, because it is the total concept, fundamentally escapes all representation.
In the succession of ecclesiastical representations it at first looks as though the spirit were subordinated to Father and Son, who, according to the expression of representation, breathe him.
But the church itself has expressly accorded to the spirit the same self-subsistence and eternity as to the two other so-called persons of the Godhead.
The spirit first is the unity without which the difference of Father and Son would be senseless or, if it had a sense, would have to lead to dualism.
Hegel therefore, in order to present the reciprocity of the mediation of the persons, threw himself about in the strangest expressions.
He also makes use here of the ecclesiastical form of the kingdom of the Father, the Son, and the Spirit, which he later retained in his philosophy of religion.
Love would, according to him, be a more adequate, more understandable expression for the concept of God, but spirit is deeper.
zh: 在这个意义上，这项工作对黑格尔来说也许是可怕至极、同时也最有成果的一次努力。
他靠自己在伯尔尼的著作，从对基督教的种种歪曲所怀的最尖刻的愤慨，又重新挣扎到了对基督教及其基本表象的信任。
他现在要在三角形的三角形中以概念把握三位一体。
他现在不想把信仰数百年来在其中崇敬自己最高财富的那种表象，当作无理性的东西从自己身边推开。
与中世纪的德意志神秘主义者及其深奥语言的相识，加强了这一方向。
早在瑞士时期结束时，黑格尔的文件里就可以找到他从各种文学报上抄下来的埃克哈特大师和陶勒的语句摘录。
但是，当他一头扎进诺斯替教时，精神的概念就作为这样的东西迎面挤向他：它因为是总体概念，在根本上逃避一切表象。
在教会表象的先后次序中，起初看来好像是精神从属于父与子，而按照表象的说法，父与子呼出精神。
但教会自己已经明确地承认精神与神性的另外两个所谓位格具有同样的独立性和永恒性。
只有精神才是那种统一性，没有它，父与子的差别就会没有意义，或者，假如这差别有意义，就必然导致二元论。
因此，黑格尔为了展示诸位格相互中介的相互性，就在最古怪的说法里四处翻滚。
他在这里还使用了父、子、精神的国度这一教会形式，这一形式他后来在宗教哲学中保留了下来。
在他看来，爱对于上帝的概念来说会是一个更贴切、更易懂的说法，但精神据说要更深。

en: In the son God cognizes himself as God.
He says to himself: I am God.
Being-within-self ceases to be a negative.
The distinguishing and the wealth of God's self-consciousness is therein reconciled with its simplicity, and the kingdom of the son of God is wholly also the kingdom of the father.

God's self-consciousness is not a returning-into-self and not an other-being of the son, nor an other-being of the returning-into-self in contrast to the simple God, but the intuition in the son is the intuiting of the same as itself, yet in such a way that the son remains son, as the undistinguished and at the same time the distinguished; or the spread-out kingdom of the universe, which no longer has any being-for-self over against itself, but whose being-for-self is a returning into God, which is God's returning into himself, a joy over the glory of the son, whom he intuits as himself.
The earth thereby, in that its being-within-self is no longer the pure being-for-self, the evil, also ceases to be a mixed thing.
What stands over against the son, who intuits the earth, in his glory, is God's glory itself, the look back and the homecoming to him.
And for the hallowed earth this self-consciousness of God is the spirit that proceeds from God and in which she [is] one with him and with the son.
This spirit is here the eternal mediator between the son returned to the father, who is now wholly only one, and the being of the son in himself, or the glory of the universe.

The simplicity of the all-embracing spirit has now stepped into the middle, and there is now no more distinguishing; for the earth, as God's self-consciousness, is now the spirit, but it is also the eternal son, whom God intuits as himself, and both are a unity and the cognition of God in himself.
Thus the holy triangle of triangles has closed itself.
The first is the idea of God, which is carried out in the other triangles and through them returns into itself.
zh: “在儿子里面，上帝把自己认识为上帝。
他对自己说：我是上帝。
在自身之内不再是一个否定的东西。
区分和上帝的自我意识的丰富性，在其中与它的单纯性得到了和解，而上帝儿子的国度也完全是父亲的国度。
上帝的自我意识不是一种返回自身之内，也不是儿子的他在，同样不是返回自身之内相对于单纯的上帝而言的他在，而是儿子中的直观就是对这同一个东西作为它自身的直观，但这样，即儿子仍然是儿子：作为无区分的、同时又是有区分的东西；或者说，那铺展开来的宇宙的国度，它不再有任何自为存在与自己相对而立，而它的自为存在是一种返回上帝之中，这返回就是上帝返回自身，是一种对儿子荣耀的喜悦，上帝把这儿子作为自己本身来直观。
大地由此，由于它的在自身之内的存在不再是纯粹的自为存在、不再是恶，也就不再是一个混合的东西。
在荣耀中与直观着大地的儿子相对而立的，是上帝自己的荣耀，是回望和向他归家。
而对于被圣化的大地来说，上帝的这种自我意识就是那从上帝出发的精神，大地在这精神中与他、与儿子[是]同一的。
这个精神在这里就是那永恒的中介者，处在已返回父亲的儿子——他现在完全只是单一者——与儿子在自身之中的存在、或宇宙的荣耀之间。
包罗一切的精神的单纯性现在已进入中项，现在不再有任何区分；因为大地作为上帝的自我意识如今就是精神，但它也是永恒的儿子，上帝把这儿子作为自己本身来直观，而两者是一个统一体，也是上帝在自身之中的认识。
神圣的三角形的三角形就这样闭合了。
第一个是上帝的观念，它在其他三角形中得到展开，并穿过它们而返回自身之中。”

en: In this first one, which at the same time is only one side of the absolute, unified triangle, only the divinity is with itself in reciprocal intuition and cognition.
It is its idea, in which the pure light of unity is the middle, and whose side is likewise the pure shining-forth and the pure bending-back of the rays into itself.
zh: “在这个第一个里，它同时只是那绝对的、统一的三角形的一条边，只有神性与自己处在交互直观和认识之中。
它是神性的观念，在这观念里统一性的纯粹光是中项，而这个观念的边同样是纯粹的向外照射和光线向自身之内的纯粹回折。”

en: In the second, God's intuition has stepped onto the one side.
He has entered into relation with evil, and the middle is the bad element of the mixture of both.
But this triangle becomes a quadrangle, in that the pure divinity hovers over it.

But even so its misfortune does not allow it to remain this triangle, but it must tip over into its opposite, the son must pass through the earth, overcome the evil and, in stepping as victor onto the one side, awaken the other, God's self-cognition, as a new cognition that is one with God, as the spirit of God: whereby the middle becomes a beautiful, free, divine middle, God's universe. - This second triangle, as being in separation, is herewith itself a twofold triangle, or its two sides are each a triangle, the one the inverted one of the other, and the middle is in this movement of history the all-effecting power of absolute unity, which hovers over the first and takes it up into itself and transforms it in itself into another.
But what is visible is the two triangles; the middle, however, is only the invisible power working within.
zh: “在第二个里，上帝的直观已经站到了一边。
他与恶发生了关系，而中项是两者混合的坏东西。
但这个三角形变成一个四边形，由于纯粹的神性悬浮在它上方。

但它的不幸即使这样也不容许它保持为这个三角形，而是它必须翻转到它的对立面中去，儿子必须穿过大地，克服恶，并且在作为胜利者站到一边时，唤醒另一边，即上帝对自身的认识，作为一种新的、与上帝为一的认识，作为上帝的精神：由此中项成为一个美的、自由的、神性的中项，成为上帝的宇宙。 - 这第二个三角形，作为处在分离之中的东西，由此本身是一个双重的三角形，或者说它的两个边各自是一个三角形，一个是另一个的倒转，而中项在这场历史的运动中就是绝对统一性那造成一切的力量，它悬浮在第一个之上，把这第一个接纳到自身之中，并在自身中把它变成另一个。
但可见的东西就是那两个三角形，而中项只是那不可见的、在内部起作用的力量。”

en: But through the second triangle of the second, the third has immediately formed itself, the return of everything into God himself, or the being-poured-out of the idea over everything.
What was only a mixture is through this spirit absolutely one with God, and as he cognizes himself in it, so it cognizes itself in God.
zh: “但通过第二个三角形的第二个三角形，第三个三角形直接就形成了，即一切返回上帝自身之中，或者说观念倾泻在一切之上。
那曾经只是一种混合的东西，通过这个精神与上帝绝对地为一，正如上帝在这个精神中认识自己，它也在上帝之中认识自己。”

en: This triangular construction has now also been carried through nature by Hegel in the particular, though with frequent abandonment of the presupposed representation and with a peculiar mixture of purely logical and figurative designations.
The sun is called the negative unity of its system.

The earth is to produce the opposition of air and water, and indeed in such a way that they do not lazily part from one another, but that they express the opposed on themselves and destroy themselves, air fattens itself with water, water with air, and at the same time both are thereby so stretched that they come to the point of springing apart, each passing over into its opposite, and so on. - Even in later years Hegel still occasionally made use of the triangular schema.
zh: 这种三角形的建构现在还被黑格尔在特殊的东西中进一步贯穿自然施行了一遍，不过常常离开那被预设的表象，并且奇特地混合了纯粹逻辑的和形象的名称。
太阳被称为它的系统的否定的统一性。
大地应当产生空气和水的对立，而且是这样：它们并不懒散地彼此分开，而是它们把对立面在它们自己身上表达出来并毁灭自己，空气用水、水用空气来喂肥自己，同时两者由此被绷得那么紧，以致到了就要跳开的地步，每一个都要过渡到它的对立面中去，等等。 - 即使在后来的年月里，黑格尔也仍然时不时使用这种三角形的图式。

en: Böttiger253) speaks of Pausanias the legend-monger, of blowing Fame with her trumpet-cheeks; but both are he himself.
zh: 伯特格尔253)说的是传说编凑者保萨尼阿斯，说的是吹着喇叭腮的声名女神；但两者都是他自己。

en: A whole series of Locrians hanged themselves for the sake of coy boys.
Greek love of boys is still little comprehended.
There lies in it a noble spurning of woman, and it points to this, that a god was to be born anew.254)
zh: 有一整串洛克里人为了那些冷淡难近的少年的缘故上吊自杀了。
希腊的少年之爱至今还很少被以概念把握。
这里面有一种对女人的高贵的鄙弃，并且指向这一点：有一个神要重新诞生。254)

en: A party is [a party] when it falls apart within itself.
So it is with Protestantism, whose differences are now to converge in attempts at union; — a proof that it no longer is.
For in falling apart the inner difference constitutes itself as reality.

At the emergence of Protestantism all the schisms of Catholicism had ceased. — Now the truth of the Christian religion is forever being proved, one does not know for whom; for after all we do not have to do with the Turks.
zh: 一个党派是在它自身中分裂的时候才成其为党派的。
新教也是如此，它的种种差别如今要在联合的尝试中合到一起；——这是一个证明，说明它已经不再存在了。
因为在分裂中，内在的差别把自己建构为实在性。
在新教产生的时候，天主教的一切分裂都已停止。——如今基督教宗教的真理不断地被证明，人们不知道是向谁证明；因为我们毕竟不是跟土耳其人打交道。

en: "To stick a tobacco pipe into a face or into a physiognomy."
Is this not poetry?

The wholly individual, at which the pipe is aimed and in which it appears, is here posited quite objectively as nothing subjective that would still have something behind it, like a drawing on a wall, — and likewise the hand that is to connect the pipe with it.
I have heard that expression from thoroughly prosaic merchants.
zh: “把一支烟斗插到脸上，或者插到面相上。”
这难道不是诗吗？
那完全个别的东西，也就是烟斗所指向并在其中出现的东西，在这里被完全客观地设定为不是什么主观的东西，不是背后还藏着一点什么的东西，就像墙上的一幅画，——那只把烟斗和它连接起来的手也同样如此。
那个说法我是从一些再平庸不过的商人那里听来的。

en: What is not called science nowadays!
"The terrace-maker, or the whole of the art of terracing."
Thus peat-cutting, chimney-building, cattle-breeding etc. as science.
zh: 如今什么东西不被叫作科学啊！
“筑台工，或者说筑台术的整体。”
于是泥炭采挖、烟囱砌筑、养牛等等都作为科学。

en: "A boy that has been in subjection."
Sommers Novellen S. 391.
Is that not the participium aoristi of the Greeks?
zh: “一个曾经被制服过的少年。”
Sommers Novellen S. 391.
这不就是希腊人的 participium aoristi 吗？

en: Experience.

The shadow that the candle-light projects, illuminated by the daylight of morning, becomes blue; the shadow that daylight casts (which is weaker, and to let which arise one must move away from the light), lit by candle-light, becomes red. — The shadow cast by candle-light, held quite close to the light, shimmers toward the greenish.
zh: 经验。
蜡烛光投下的影子，被早晨的日光一照，就变成蓝色；日光投下的影子（它更弱，而要让它出现，人就得离开光源），被蜡烛光一照，就变成红色。——蜡烛光投下的影子，紧挨着光拿着，就泛出偏向绿的光泽。

en: On historical logic.
It is asserted that we judge: gold is yellow.
This assurance is probable.
But it is not equally probable that we infer: all men are mortal: Cajus is a man; therefore he is mortal.
I at least have never thought such flat stuff.
It is supposed to go on inwardly, without our having consciousness of it.
To be sure, much goes on inwardly, e.g. the production of urine and something still worse, but when it becomes outward, we hold our nose.
Likewise with such inferring.
zh: 论历史逻辑。
有人断言说，我们这样判断：金子是黄的。
这个断言很可能是真的。
但并不同样很可能为真的是：我们这样推论：所有人都会死：卡尤斯是人；所以他会死。
至少我从来没有想过这么浅薄无聊的东西。
据说它在内部发生，而我们对此并没有意识。
当然，内部发生的事情很多，例如尿的生成，还有比这更糟的，可它一旦变成外在的，我们就捂住鼻子。
这样的推论也一样。

en: The older Germans were really a merry folk.
Out of the worthy Ulysses, whose life is an earnestness, they made a silly Eulenspiegel, out of the divine Circe, appearing in her as Nemesis, a pig.
The more recent ones do more or less the same, only with greater earnestness.
Formerly the people was the irony over those divine beings, but now these are the irony over the earnest handlers and conceivers.
zh: 早先的德意志人其实是个爱逗乐的民族。
他们把可敬的尤利西斯——他的生活就是一种严肃——变成了一个傻乎乎的奥伊伦施皮格尔，把神性的基尔克——她在那里以涅墨西斯的身份出现——变成了一头猪。
较晚近的人或多或少做着同样的事，只是更加严肃。
从前民众是对那些神性存在者的反讽，如今这些神性存在者倒成了对认真的处理者和以概念把握者的反讽。

en: As there has been a poetic period of genius, so at present there seems to be the philosophical period of genius.

Some carbon, oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen kneaded together and stuck into a paper described by others with polarity etc., with a wooden pigtail of vanity etc. firing rockets into the air, they think they are representing the empyrean.
So Görres, Wagner255) and others. The crudest empiricism with a formalism of substances and poles, trimmed with reasonless analogies and drunken flashes of thought.
zh: 正如曾经有过一个诗的天才时代，目前看来就是一个哲学的天才时代。
把一些碳、氧、氮和氢揉在一起，塞进一张被别人用极性等等写过的纸里，带着一根虚荣的木头发辫等等朝空中射火箭，他们就以为这是在呈现最高天。
戈雷斯、瓦格纳255)等人就是这样。最粗糙的经验，加上一种关于质料和极的形式主义，再拿无理性的类比和醉醺醺的思想闪光来镶边。

en: The peasant woman lives in the circle of her Liese, who is her best cow, then of the black one, the brindled one etc.; also of Märtel, her boy, also of Urschel, her girl, and so forth.
Such familiar things are, for the philosopher, infinity, cognition, motion, the laws of sense, and so forth.
And just as the peasant woman's deceased brother and uncle, so for the philosopher Plato, Spinoza and so forth.
The one has as much actuality as the other, but the latter have eternity in advance.
zh: 农妇活在她的莉泽，也就是她最好的那头母牛，然后是黑妞、花妞等等的圈子里；也活在她的男孩梅尔滕、她的女孩乌舍尔的圈子里，等等。
对哲学家来说，无限性、认识、运动、感性的法则等等，就是这样家常的东西。
而正如农妇的死去的兄弟和叔叔，哲学家的柏拉图、斯宾诺莎等等也是如此。
这一个和那一个有同样多的现实性，但后者多出了永恒。

en: With the husks, people are already in science.
From there it is not far to the pater peccavi.
zh: 在豆荚那里，人就已经处在科学中了。
从那儿到 pater peccavi 就不远了。

en: Is it only the German women who let the Frenchwomen give them laws? - The German gentlemen too, you say in reply, Madame, and appeal to the story of the Imperial Deputation. - You do not know the story?
Oh, I must tell it to you.
The German Empire is assured by the French that it is waging war with them.
It has, to be sure, no hand on the weapons, apart from a couple of philistines who are not to be counted for anything.
But the French have assured it, and since these assured it, one accordingly had to let oneself be plundered.
Then the German Empire learned from the newspapers - we read them at table, and you can imagine what joy it caused that this was said of it -, that it had made peace.
But so that it might know in what manner the peace stood - the French are polite people -, they sent a special envoy to Germany to tell it so.
So that there could be no doubt, he took yet another one along with him.
The Germans, as honest people - out of the mouth of two witnesses the truth becomes known - naturally believed it when these assured it.
They too are polite and thanked handsomely for it.
zh: 难道只有德意志妇女让法国女人给自己立法律？——德意志的先生们也一样，您这么反驳说，夫人，还援引帝国代表会议那段历史为证。——您不知道那段历史？
哦，那我得给您讲一讲。
德意志帝国得到法国人的保证，说它在跟他们打仗。
它固然没有把手放在武器上，除了几个根本不算数的市侩。
但法国人已经这样保证了，而既然他们这样保证，那就只得任凭自己被抢劫一空。
随后德意志帝国从报纸上得知——我们是在饭桌旁读的，您可以想见，这话说到它头上时引起了多大的欢喜——，它已经缔结了和约。
可是为了让它知道这和平是怎么一回事——法国人是讲礼貌的人——，他们还特地派了一个使节到德意志去，把这事告诉它。
为了让人没法怀疑，他又给自己添了一个。
德意志人作为老实人——真理是从两个见证人的口中显明出来的——，在这些人作保证时自然就信了。
他们也很讲礼貌，为此体面地道了谢。

en: If the absolute slips and falls out of the ground, where it strolls about, into the water, then it becomes a fish, an organic thing, a living thing.

If it now likewise slips and falls into pure thinking - for pure thinking too is not to be its ground -, then, plumping into it, it is supposed to become something bad, something finite, of which one really must be ashamed to speak, if it did not happen by virtue of office and because after all it cannot be denied that a logic is there.
Water is such a cold, bad element, and yet life is so well off in it.
Is thinking, then, to be a much worse element?
Is the absolute to feel so very bad in it and also to behave so badly in it?
zh: 如果绝对者滑了一下，从它四处溜达的土地上掉进水里，那么它就成了一条鱼，一个有机的东西，一个活的东西。
如果它现在也同样滑了一下，掉进纯粹思维里——因为纯粹思维也不该是它的土地——，那么它扑通一声掉进去，就该变成某种坏的、有限的东西，说起这种东西，人本来就该感到羞耻，要不是职务在身，要不是因为毕竟无法否认有一种逻辑在那里。
水是那么冷、那么坏的一种元素，可生命在里面却那么舒服。
难道思维就该是糟糕得多的一种元素吗？
难道绝对者就该在里面觉得那么糟，而且举止也那么糟吗？

en: In Germany sound common sense is forever being taken under protection against the so-called presumptions of philosophy.
Vain effort, for even if philosophy concedes everything to them, it is still of no use to them, for — they have none.

Genuine sound common sense is not boorish coarseness, but in the cultivated sphere a free and violent dealing with the determinacies of culture according to truth, and then immediately Rousseauian paradox, when it expresses its contradiction against the determinacies, just as culture itself does, in fundamental propositions, or as experience, reasoning, wit, like Voltaire or Helvetius.
The nobility in Germany indeed has sound common sense too, but precisely for that reason it needs it outright, without proving that it may be used — and it is at this that those others stop short.
zh: 在德意志，人们总是把健全常识保护起来，用它来对抗哲学所谓的僭妄。
白费力气，因为就算哲学对他们什么都让步，对他们也还是没有一点用处，因为——他们根本就没有。
真正的健全常识不是乡巴佬的粗野，而是在有教养的圈子里自由而粗暴地按照真理对待教养的各种规定性，随后立刻就是卢梭式的悖论，如果它像教养本身一样，把自己针对那些规定性的矛盾用根本命题表达出来，或者表现为经验、推理、机智，像伏尔泰或爱尔维修那样。
德意志的贵族固然也有健全常识，但正因如此，他们干脆就需要它，而不去证明它可以被使用——而那些人恰恰就停在这一点上。

en: Wieland, whom one otherwise precisely does not accuse of paradox, has put forward the paradoxical proposition that it is useful to understand something of the matter one writes about, and people have found it sound.
zh: 维兰德平常恰恰没人指责他爱发悖论，他却提出了这样一个悖论式的命题，即对自己所写的题材多少懂一点是有益的，而人们发现这个命题很靠得住。

en: Fools grow wise through harm; clever people, by contrast, remain unwise through every harm.
zh: 愚人吃了亏才变聪明，聪明人却吃尽一切亏仍旧不聪明。

en: Be no sleepyhead, but always awake!
For if you are a sleepyhead, then you are blind and dumb.
But if you are awake, you see everything and say of everything what it is.
This, however, is reason and the mastering of the world.
zh: 别做瞌睡虫，要一直醒着！
因为如果你是瞌睡虫，那你就又瞎又哑。
但你要是醒着，你就看见一切，并且对一切说出它是什么。
而这也就是理性，是对世界的支配。

en: On coins of Titus and Vespasian: ϑειότης, aeternitas (Titi etc.) something common.
Also already Aeternitas Augusti.
Imperial title: Aeternitas vestra. Αἰώνιος βίος also occurs from the Ptolemies on the Rosetta Stone; otherwise also only αἰώνιος.
This αἰών otherwise seemed to be peculiar to the New Testament.
zh: 在提图斯和韦斯帕芗的钱币上：ϑειότης、aeternitas（Titi 等等）很平常。
Aeternitas Augusti 也早就有了。
皇帝的称号：Aeternitas vestra。Αἰώνιος βίος 也出现在罗塞塔石碑上的托勒密诸王那里；别处也只有 αἰώνιος。
这个 αἰών 从前显得是《新约》所独有的东西。

en: To a scrupulous person one can say that conscience is a moral lantern that shines only on a good path; if one walks on an evil one, one blows it out.
zh: 对一个疑虑重重的人，可以说良心是一盏道德的灯笼，它只在好路上照亮；要是走在坏路上，人就会把它吹灭。

en: In omnia alia abeunt — these people, who with the denial of their subjectivity are to think and accept something proven, truth.
Their subjective unrest is not capable of the calm of cognition.
They have stood under no discipline.
zh: In omnia alia abeunt，这些人应当以否认自己的主观性去思维并接受某种已被证明的东西，即真理。
他们主观上的不安，达不到认识的那种安宁。
他们从来没有受过任何管教。

en: In Swabia one says of something long since past: it is so long ago that it will soon no longer be true.
Thus Christ died for our sins so long ago that it will soon no longer be true.
zh: 在施瓦本，人们对早就发生的事说：它已经过去这么久了，快要不再是真的了。
基督为我们的罪而死也已经这么久了，快要不再是真的了。

en: The balls, public places, spectacles are no longer much visited.
On s'assemble en famille, on revient aux mœurs.
These mœurs are the general boredom of the public, morality.
zh: 舞会、公共场所、戏剧，去的人已经不多了。
On s'assemble en famille, on revient aux mœurs.
这些 mœurs 就是公共领域普遍的无聊，即道德。

en: For baseness, morality is possible only as a relation to virtue.
As Karl Moor, after he has utterly despaired, after father and beloved are gone, goes to his punishment through a moral action: "The man can be helped."
The truly tragic is the moral.
To us it is at the same time sentimental.
zh: 对卑劣来说，只有作为与美德之关系的道德才是可能的。
就像卡尔·莫尔，在他彻底绝望之后，在父亲和恋人都不在了之后，通过一件道德的行为走向自己的惩罚：“这个人还可以救。”
真正悲剧性的东西就是道德的东西。
对我们来说，它同时又是感伤的。

en: The truth of science is a calm light that illuminates and gladdens everything, as well as a warmth in which everything at the same time sprouts prosperously and lays out the inner treasures in the breadth of life.
The flash of thought is Capaneus, who imitates this heavenly fire in a bad, vanishing way, formally destructive, and is able to arrive at no subsisting life.
zh: 科学的真理是一种平静的、照亮并愉悦一切的光，同时也是一种温暖，在它里面一切都同时茂盛地冒出来，并把内在的财富在生命的广度中铺展开来。
思想的闪电是卡帕纽斯，他以一种坏的、消逝着的方式模仿这天上之火，只在形式上加以毁灭，而绝不能达到任何持存着的生命。

en: If one knows the Pythagorean theorem and says: one can neither eat nor drink by it; - another: what is that to me? what matters is application to life; I must find my totality expressed in it; - a third: no practical use, no maxim of wisdom for the moral life comes out of it; - then all this is one, but we honour the expression in such a way that we call the first boorish churlishness, the second sound common sense, the third zeal for the moral interest of humankind.
zh: 如果一个人懂得毕达哥拉斯定理，却说：靠它并不能吃也不能喝；——另一个人说：这跟我有什么关系？要紧的是对生活的应用；我必须在这上面看到我的总体性被表达出来；——第三个人说：从这里得不出任何实际用处，得不出给道德生活的智慧箴言；——那么这一切都是一回事，但我们如此敬重这种说法，以致我们把第一种叫作粗鲁的土气，把第二种叫作健全常识，把第三种叫作对人类的道德利益的热情。

en: "Que de choses dans un menuet! s'écriait Marcel, le plus fameux maître de danse de Paris, il y a quatorze ans, dans l'enthousiasme de son art. Les danseurs d'aujourd'hui disent autrement: il faut savoir le moral de la danse, et ils disent cela très serieusement."
In Germany this is called: poetry.
zh: “Que de choses dans un menuet! s'écriait Marcel, le plus fameux maître de danse de Paris, il y a quatorze ans, dans l'enthousiasme de son art. Les danseurs d'aujourd'hui disent autrement: il faut savoir le moral de la danse, et ils disent cela très serieusement.”
在德意志，这叫作：诗。

en: "L'empire germanique est un être moral sans action par lui même, et il est un corps, mort par sa constitution."
Germany is no monarchy etc., no state, but a realm.
Realm is supposed to be a concept, or rather, if it is supposed to be state, an intuition that is empty.
zh: “L'empire germanique est un être moral sans action par lui même, et il est un corps, mort par sa constitution.”
德意志不是君主国等等，不是国家，而是一个帝国。
帝国应当是一个概念，或者更确切地说，如果它应当是国家，就是一个空洞的直观。

en: The Allgemeine Zeitung reports from Frau v. Staël in Berlin how the Queen addressed her: "J'espère, Madame, que Vous nous croyez de trop bon gout, pour n'être pas flatté de Vôtre arrivée à Berlin.
Il y a longtemps, que je Vous ai admirée, et j'aiété impatiente, de faire Vôtre connaissance."
Here too, after all, spirit came to spirit, and like gladly joins like, as the proverb says.
zh: 《总汇报》从柏林报道施塔埃尔夫人，说王后是这样跟她打招呼的：“J'espère, Madame, que Vous nous croyez de trop bon gout, pour n'être pas flatté de Vôtre arrivée à Berlin.
Il y a longtemps, que je Vous ai admirée, et j'aiété impatiente, de faire Vôtre connaissance.”
这里毕竟也是精神遇上了精神，而正如谚语所说，相似者乐意与相似者结伴。

en: In the German treatments of the sciences the content of most works is only this: I too know what has been invented here or there.
Thus six hundred have treated the cowpox, and all repeated the same thing.

They then fell into dispute with one another over plagiarism, but the fact of the matter was that they had all copied the same thing, just as the Evangelists are supposed not to have copied from one another, but to have had one Gospel before them.
In free sciences, such as philosophy, everyone copies down the general triviality of culture.
zh: 在德意志人对各门科学的处理中，大多数作品的内容只是这一点：这个或那个被人发明出来的东西，我也知道。
于是有六百人处理过牛痘，而所有人都重复了同样的东西。
他们随后就为剽窃彼此争执起来，但事情的真相是：他们全都抄了同一个东西，就像福音书作者们并不是互相抄写，而是据说面前摆着一部福音书。
在哲学这样的自由科学里，每个人都抄下教养的一般平庸之物。

en: The answer that Robespierre gave to everything - here one had thought this, done that, willed this or said that - was: la mort!
Its uniformity is supremely boring, but it fits everything.
You want the coat: here you have it; the waistcoat too: here; you give a slap on the cheek: here is the other cheek too; you want the little finger: cut it off.
I can kill everything, abstract from everything.
Thus obstinacy is unconquerable and can overcome everything in itself.
But the highest thing there would be to overcome would be precisely this freedom, this death itself.
zh: 罗伯斯庇尔对一切给出的回答——这里有人想到了这个、做了那个，意欲了这个或说了那个——就是：la mort！
它的千篇一律极其无聊，但它适用于一切。
你们要外套：给你们；背心也一样：在这儿；你们打一记耳光：另一边脸也在这儿；你们要那根小指头：就把它砍下来。
我可以杀死一切，可以抽掉一切。
所以固执是无法克服的，并且能在它自己身上克服一切。
但真正要被克服的最高者，恰恰就是这种自由，就是这死亡本身。

en: Reading the newspaper early in the morning is a kind of realist morning blessing.
One orients one's bearing toward the world on God or on what the world is.
The former gives the same certainty as the latter, namely that one knows how one stands with it.
zh: 清晨读报是一种实在论的晨祷。
人把自己面对世界的态度定位于上帝，或者定位于世界所是的东西。
前者给出的确定性和后者一样，就是人知道自己跟它处在什么关系上。

en: Ora et labora!
Pray and curse!
Cursing is otherwise when someone says sacrament, but in religion all these things, which are otherwise outside one another, fall together.
The earth be cursed, and in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat thy bread!
To work means to destroy the world or to curse.
zh: Ora et labora！
祈祷，并诅咒！
诅咒平时是说一个人口出圣事的时候，但在宗教里，所有这些平时彼此在外的说法都合到一起。
地必受诅咒，你必汗流满面才得吃你的面包！
工作就意味着毁灭世界，或者说诅咒。

en: Necessity of studying a system of philosophy through and through.
The principle contains everything wrapped up, but also only wrapped up, latent, the empty formal concept, not the matter itself.
As a miser keeps all enjoyments in his purse as possibility and spares himself the actuality, the burdensomeness of enjoyment itself.
zh: 把一种哲学体系完整地研究一遍的必要性。
原则把一切都裹在里面包含着，但也只是裹着、潜在地包含，包含的是空洞的形式概念，而不是事情本身。
就像一个吝啬鬼在钱袋里把一切享受都作为可能性保留着，而给自己省掉了现实性，省掉了享受本身的辛苦。

en: The questions which philosophy does not answer are answered in such a way that they ought not to be put that way.
zh: 哲学没有回答的那些问题，是这样得到回答的：它们本来就不该那样被提出。

en: Gellert, Hagedorn, Utz have flatly rhymed virtue: 'Who only loves virtue' etc.
True, I found it, between virtue and understanding etc.
Friend, virtue is no empty name etc.
God forbid! - Nicolai, a bookseller in Berlin, thereupon invented uprightness, or chiefly urged it.
zh: 盖勒特、哈格多恩、乌茨把美德写成了平淡的韵文：“谁只要爱美德”等等。
诚然，我找到了它，在美德与知性之间，等等。
朋友，美德不是空洞的名字，等等。
上帝不容！——柏林的书商尼古拉，接着就发明了正直，或者主要是大力鼓吹了它。

en: It is a fine trait, what contempt for money one has and shows in Germany.
The Germans ascribe to it an origin that cannot be more contemptible and low.
One represents it for the eye in figures that are called Geldsch-r.
A mythological relation is supposed to underlie it.
One does not like to think a bratwurst, or whatever it may be, together with such a low manner of origin.
zh: 这是一个美好的特点：在德意志，人们对金钱怀着并且表现出怎样的鄙视。
德意志人给它编造了一个再鄙劣、再低贱不过的起源。
人们把它画成给眼睛看的图形，这些图形叫做 Geldsch-r。
这背后应该有一个神话上的关联。
一根烤肠或者随便什么，人们总不愿把它和这样一种低贱的产生方式放在一起想。

en: Ordinary thinking does not construct: here a lime tree next to willows, cuttings, etc., and below a cow walks past.
It does not prove, but takes its effort as proof of something, boredom as depth, and its exhaustion as the result.
zh: 平庸的思维不建构：这儿一棵椴树挨着柳树、插枝等等，下面还有一头牛走过。
它不证明，而是把自己的费力当作对某事物的证明，把无聊当作深刻，把自己的疲惫当作结果。

en: What has a deep meaning is for that very reason good for nothing.
zh: 凡是有深刻含义的东西，恰恰因此毫无用处。

en: Our posterity is the next fair.
As in reason everything draws together, so too in a mountain view the river draws nearer.
Pedes eorum, qui efferent te, sunt ante ianuam. (The feet of those who will carry you out are before the door.)
zh: 我们的后世就是下一届博览会。
正如在理性中一切都聚拢到一起，在山景中，河流也靠得更近。
Pedes eorum, qui efferent te, sunt ante ianuam.（那些要把你带出去的人的脚就在门前。）

en: Science.
Whether the individual possesses it, he can assure himself and others.
Whether it is true, the nearest surroundings decide, the contemporary world and then posterity, if the former have already given their assent.
But consciousness has risen so in culture, the barbaric toughness of conceiving has become more fluid and quicker, that a few years already bring posterity on.
Over Kantian philosophy the staff has long been broken, while the Wolffian held out fifty and more years.
More swiftly has the determining of its standpoint hurried on for Fichte's philosophy.
What Schelling's philosophy is in its essence, a short time will reveal.
The judgment upon it stands, as it were, before the door, for many already understand it.
But these philosophies succumbed less to proof than to the empirical experience of how far one can get with them.
Blindly they train their followers, but the web grows ever thinner, and at last they find themselves surprised by the spider-web's transparency.
It has melted away from them like ice and run through their fingers like quicksilver, without their knowing what was happening to them.
They simply no longer have it, and whoever looks into their hand, with which they offered their wisdom for sale, sees nothing but the empty hand and goes on with mockery.
While those who feel the cold still proclaim it to be something, these suppose they have fathomed the matter, whereas they only glimpse the nothingness of it, not what it was.
The one part is deceived as the other.
The true, however, is that this vanished thing itself has brought them hither.
The word of Scripture is fulfilled: if we are silent, the stones cry out.
zh: 科学。
个人是否拥有科学，他可以对自己也对别人保证。
它是不是真的，要由最近的周遭、同时代的人，然后是后世来决定，如果前两者已经表示过赞同的话。
但意识在教养中已经提升到这样的地步，以概念把握的那种野蛮的顽固已经变得更流畅、更迅速，以至于短短几年就把后世带到了眼前。
对康德哲学早已宣判完毕，而沃尔夫的哲学却维持了五十年甚至更久。
对费希特哲学来说，确定其立场来得更快。
谢林哲学在本质上是什么，短时间就会显露出来。
对它的判决可以说已经站在门口了，因为许多人已经理解它了。
不过这些哲学与其说败给了证明，不如说败给了经验上的体会：人们用它们究竟能走多远。
它们盲目地培养信徒，但那张网越织越薄，最后它们发现自己被蜘蛛网般的透明弄得措手不及。
它对他们来说像冰一样融化了，像水银一样从指缝里流走了，他们却不知道自己是怎么了。
他们就是不再拥有它了，谁要是看看他们那只用来兜售智慧的手，看到的就只是一只空手，于是带着嘲笑走开。
当那些感到寒冷的人还把它称作某种东西时，这些人却自以为已经把这件事弄透了，而他们看到的其实只是这件事的无，不是它曾经是什么。
一方和另一方一样受了骗。
而真相是，这个已经消失的东西本身把他们带到了这里。
经上的话就应验了：我们若沉默，石头就要喊叫。

en: The first subjective thing in the study of the sciences is honesty toward oneself.
To doubt everything is easily thought and easily said, but the question is whether it is true?
The empty word, if the whole nature of the essence does not deny itself, is a lie, and it is frightful what people want to lie to themselves and others about and to talk them into.
zh: 研究各门科学时，第一个主观的东西就是对自己的诚实。
怀疑一切都是容易想到、也容易说出的，但问题在于：它是不是真的？
空洞的话，如果本质的整个本性没有自我否认，就是一句谎言，而人们想要用什么来对自己和别人撒谎、想要劝自己和别人相信什么，这是可怕的。

en: For the study of a science it is necessary not to let oneself be turned away by the principles.
They are general and do not mean much.
As it seems, only he has their meaning who has the particular.
Often they are also bad.
They are the consciousness of the matter, and the matter is often better than the consciousness.
One should study on.
At first consciousness is turbid.

Only one does not want to have grasped and proved it step by step, but one throws the book away, reads on as between waking and sleeping, resigns one's consciousness, that is, one's singleness, which is painful.
That is how I studied the differential calculus and other things.
So I heard it from others who studied Kant's Critique of Pure Reason in this way.
zh: 研究一门科学，必要的是不让自己被那些原则带偏。
它们是普遍的，没有多少意味。
看来，只有拥有特殊东西的人，才拥有它们的意义。
它们还常常是糟糕的。
它们是对事情的意识，而事情常常比意识更好。
人只管继续研究下去。
起初意识是浑浊的。
只是人不想一步一步地以概念把握它并加以证明，而是把书扔掉，像在半睡半醒之间那样一直读下去，对自己的意识、也就是对自己的单一性认了命，这是难受的。
我就是这样研究微分计算和其他东西的。
也听别人说过，他们就是这样研究康德的《纯粹理性批判》的。

en: Original, quite wonderful works in culture are like a bomb that falls into a rotten city, in which everything sits over the beer mug and is extremely wise and does not feel that its flat well-being has just brought about the crashing of the thunder.
zh: 教养中那些原创的、十分奇妙的作品，就像一颗落进一座腐朽城市的炸弹，在这座城市里，所有东西都坐在啤酒杯旁，极其智慧，却感觉不到，正是他们那种平庸的安康引来了这声雷鸣。

en: The most harmful thing is to want to preserve oneself from errors.
The fear of actively creating error for oneself is the comfort and the accompaniment of absolutely passive error.
Thus the stone has no active error, except for example lime, when aqua fortis is poured on it.
Then it comes quite out of itself.
It properly goes astray, seethes up, comes into another world.
They are Bohemian villages to it, it perishes.
Not so the human being.
It is substance, it preserves itself.

This stoneness or stoniness or stoneness (for the German language has difficulty making a substantive, a thing, a solid man, a guild citizen who has wife and children, into a predicate!), it is this stubborn fluidity that one must renounce.
Formability, not the instinctive non aridet, is the truth.
Only when one understands the matter, which comes after the learning, does one stand above it.
zh: 最有害的，就是想让自己免于种种错误。
害怕主动给自己造出错误，这种害怕就是安逸，是绝对被动的错误的陪伴。
这样，石头没有主动的错误，除了比如石灰，当硝酸浇在它上面的时候。
这时它完全从自身里跑了出来。
它真就走上歧途，翻腾起来，进入另一个世界。
这些对它来说是波希米亚的村庄，它毁灭了。
人却不是这样。
它是实体，保存自身。
这种石头性、石质性或者石头般的性质（因为德语很难把一个实体、一个东西、一个结实的男人、一个有妻子儿女的行会市民变成一个谓语！），正是这种顽硬的流质，是人必须放弃的。
可教养性，而不是那种本能的 non aridet，才是真理。
只有当人懂得了事情，而这是在学之后才来的，人才站到它之上。

en: The fundamental proposition of a system of philosophy is its result.

Just as we read the last scene of a play, the last page of a novel, or as Sancho thought it better to say the solution of the riddle beforehand, so the beginning of a philosophy is indeed also its exit, which is not the case with those.

But no one will content himself with this end of those things or with the word of the riddle, but the movement through which it comes about is held to be the essential. - That the particular is in the universal, the opponents of philosophy deny, and they themselves practise this, in that they tug to and fro only at the principle, because the whole is [supposed to be] in it.
They possess the whole as they possess mathematics when they have bought a copy of Euclid or a slave who is a mathematician.
The thing itself one cannot obtain as a gift, as it were thrown in on top of the purchase, by procuring for oneself the principle or the result.
To stop at intuition, on the other hand, e.g. Jacob Böhme's, is barbarism, as at fundamental propositions it is superficiality.
The development of knowledge is not a clearing away of those intuitions, any more than of the fundamental proposition, but a shaping of them from within outwards or from outside inwards.
Böhme's intuition is a deeper one than Jacobi's faith reveals.
Those who take such a thing as a particular, vanishing opinion and place barbarism in the thing itself err just as much as those who do not hold the fundamental proposition to be essential.
The former make the form of the barbarous into the essence of the thing, the latter on the contrary the solidity of faith.
(Jacobi: we are born in faith; hand-pressing; dear Mendelssohn etc.; how empty pietists with crooked heads and twisted eyes press one another's hands, without knowing how to say anything.)
zh: 一个哲学体系的根本命题就是它的结果。
正如我们读一出戏的最后一幕、一部小说的最后一页，或者像桑丘那样认为事先把谜底说出来更好，一个哲学的开端确实也同样是它的出口，而在那些东西那里却并非如此。
但没有人会满足于那些东西的这个结尾，或者满足于谜底这句话，而是那使它得以产生的运动才被看作本质的东西。——特殊的东西在普遍的东西之中，这是哲学的反对者们所否认的，而他们自己也在这样做，因为他们只抓住原则来回拉扯，理由就是整体就在这原则里面。
他们拥有整体，就像他们买下一本欧几里得的书、或者买下一个身为数学家的奴隶时，就拥有数学一样。
人们不能因为给自己弄到了原则或结果，就把事情本身当作礼物、当作仿佛是买卖里额外搭上的东西那样得到。
相反，停留在直观上，例如停留在雅各布·波墨的直观上，是野蛮，正如停留在根本命题上是肤浅一样。
知识的发展并不是把那些直观清除掉，正如不是把根本命题清除掉一样，而是把它们从内向外或从外向内塑造出来。
波墨的直观比雅可比的信仰所启示出来的更深刻。
那些把这样的东西当作个别的、正在消逝的意见，并把野蛮放进事情本身里的人，和那些不把根本命题看作本质的人一样错。
前一种人把野蛮的形式当作事情的本质，后一种人相反，把信仰的纯正当作本质。
（雅可比：我们是在信仰中出生的；握手；亲爱的门德尔松等等；就像空疏的虔敬派信徒歪着脑袋、翻着眼睛互相握手，却不知道说什么。）

en: The barbarian is astonished when he hears that the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the two legs.
He thinks it could also be otherwise, is afraid above all of the understanding, and remains in intuition.
Reason without understanding is nothing, understanding is yet something without reason.
The understanding cannot be given as a gift.
zh: 野蛮人听到斜边的平方等于两条直角边的平方之和时，就感到惊奇。
他认为这也可能是另一个样子，尤其害怕知性，于是停留在直观里。
没有知性的理性什么也不是，没有理性的知性却还是某种东西。
知性是不能被赠送的。

en: The words eternal, holy, absolute, infinite draw the human being who feels something in them upward, warm him, heat him.
They are powers that rule him, pull him to and fro, and the sign of their dominion over him is that he feels himself in their presence.
They are the intuited gods of the Greeks, which for the northerners are only abstractions, only words, and thereby themselves in ideal form.
Only comprehending kills them as power.
It separates itself from them.
Instead of lying in their element, it is the stepping back from them and the seeing-through of them, a feelingless clarity.
Those words elevate the human being, - how much more their cognition!
But their cognition gives the human being, the I, its freedom, and the elevation is the erased heat or the (erased) feeling of the individual.
zh: 永恒、神圣、绝对、无限这些词，把在它们那里感觉到某种东西的人向上提起，使他温暖，使他发热。
它们是一些支配他、把他来回拉扯的力量，而它们统治他的标志，就是他在它们那里感觉到自己。
它们是希腊人被直观到的诸神，这些神对北方人来说只是抽象、只是词语，因此本身处在观念的形式中。
只有以概念把握才把它们作为力量杀死。
以概念把握把自己与它们分离开来。
它不是躺在它们的元素里，而是从它们那里退回来，把它们看透，是一种没有感觉的清明。
那些词提升人，——对它们的认识就更是如此！
但对它们的认识把自由给予人、给予我，而那种提升是被抹掉的灼热，或者说是个体的（被抹掉的）感觉。

en: God, having become nature, has spread himself out into the splendour and the mute cycle of the formations, becomes conscious of the expansion, of the lost punctuality, and grows wrathful over it.
The wrath is this formation, this gathering together into the empty point.

He finds himself as such, and his essence poured out into the rest- and unrestless infinity, where there is no present, but a desolate driving out beyond the limit, which always comes to be as it is sublated.
This wrath, in that it is this driving-out, is the destruction of nature.
The going out beyond the formations is likewise an absolute going into itself, a becoming toward the centre point.
In this, the wrath devours its formations into itself.
Their whole extended realm must pass through this centre point; their bones are crushed by it and their flesh squeezed into precisely this fluidity.
zh: 上帝变成了自然，把自己铺展到种种形态的壮丽和无声的循环之中，又意识到这种铺展、这种失去的点性，并为此发怒。
这种愤怒就是这种形成，就是这种向空洞的点的收拢。
他发现自己就是这样，并且发现自己的本质被倾泻进那种既不安息又不停息的无限性之中，在那里没有当下，只有一种越过界限的荒芜的向外驰骋，而这条界限总是生成着，正如它被扬弃一样。
这种愤怒，既然它就是这种向外驰骋，那就是自然的毁灭。
越过种种形态而向外走去，同样是一种绝对的走入自身，一种向中心点的生成。
在这个中心点里，这种愤怒把它的种种形态吞进自身。
它们整个广延的王国必须穿过这个中心点；它们的骨头被它碾碎，它们的肉被挤进这同一种流动状态之中。

en: The wrath of God over itself in its otherness, the fallen Lucifer, fixed here, rebels against God, and his beauty makes him arrogant.
Nature, with consciousness of its shape, displays it and takes pleasure in itself in it.

But this being-for-itself of it, or its being as consciousness, is not its being in the ever calm representation of itself, so that thought would be merely the secondary, the empty inactive space that receives its content, but this consciousness is immediately absolute activity.
It is wrath itself, the ignition of the fury in it, which wears itself away and consumes its arrogant splendour.
The consumed nature rises in a new ideal shape as a realm of shadows, which has lost that first life, the appearance of its spirit after the death of its life.
But this new shape is the overcoming of evil, the having-endured in the glow of pain at the centre, where it, purified, has left behind all the dross in the crucible, a residue that is pure nothing.
It rises as free spirit, which sees this its transfiguration only in nature. -
zh: 上帝在自身的他在中对自己的愤怒，即堕落的路西法，在这里被固定下来，它起而反抗上帝，而它的美使它变得傲慢。
自然带着对其形态的意识，把形态展示出来，并在其中自我欣赏。
但它这种自为存在，或者说它作为意识的存在，并不是它在对自身的永远平静的表象中的存在，以致思想只是次要的东西，是接受其内容的空洞而不活动的空间，而是这种意识直接就是绝对的活动。
这就是愤怒本身，是它里面怒火的点燃，这怒火自我磨损，吞噬着自己那傲慢的壮丽。
被吞噬的自然以一种新的观念形态作为影子王国升起，它已经失去了那最初的生命，是它的精神在其生命死后的显现。
但这种新形态是对恶的克服，是在中心的痛苦灼热中坚持下来的经历，在那里它经过净化，把一切浮渣都留在坩埚里，是一种残留物，而这残留物就是纯粹的无。
它作为自由的精神升起，而这精神只在自然界中看到自己这种变容。——

en: Such myths, such intuitions are the intuitions of barbarism.
The shape of these intuitions annihilates the individual, or here it is rather the fury against this Absolute that has come to be and itself again subsists.
For the individual is nothing in it.
It does not perish but has perished, and that intuition must still pass through a second process in order to be absolute.

This is science or cognition: that that imagining-into-itself, that life-course of God, proceeds out of cognition itself; that nature in its essence is not the otherness at which the spirit, that it has thus lost itself, is enraged, but that its intuition, it as itself, is spirit.
The individual as such is itself nature, and the intuition of the divine essence a natural one, even if its content is spirit.
The individual itself goes this way in the consuming of itself or in science, for in the latter the natural essence of the subject perishes.

And it is not merely the elevation of the individual to it or a culture of the same; it is not merely a regard from its side, a relation to it: but the second cycle of the Absolute itself, which, having become spirit, as such, as a totality brought forth, as spirit, as consciousness, enters into that pain, so that the spirit as consciousness produces that its becoming on itself as on one that has become. - That intuition of religion is universal religion, and it is this only as science.

Not a passing-through, a producing of that first path within itself as an intuiting cycle; but science raises itself above faith and its intuiting, leaves itself as spirit and comes to itself as spirit.

The culture, the scientific development of that intuition is this: that it always remains spirit, does not lose spirit, and as this spirit that does not lose itself becomes an other to itself and finds itself again.

Knowledge makes every moment of intuition, which for itself is an impenetrable, determinate shape that does not open up its inner being but comes forth, acts and vanishes through another that acts, into a process within itself or into a spiritual nature.
zh: 这样的神话，这样的直观，都是野蛮状态的直观。
这些直观的形态把个体消灭掉，或者说，这里其实是针对这个已经生成、又自行持存的绝对者的怒火。
因为个体在其中什么也不是。
它不是在毁灭，而是已经毁灭了，而那直观还必须再经过第二个过程，才能成为绝对的。
这第二过程就是科学或认识：那种向自身之内的想象，那种上帝的生命历程，是从认识本身中产生出来的；自然在其本质中并不是精神因自己如此丧失而对其发怒的他在，而是它的直观，即作为它自身的它，就是精神。
个体作为个体本身就是自然，而对神圣本质的直观也是一种自然的直观，尽管它的内容是精神。
个体自己走这条路，是在自我吞噬中，或是在科学中，因为在科学中，主体的自然本质归于消亡。
而这并不只是个体向它的提升，或者个体的一种教养；也不只是从它这方面来的一种看重，一种对它的关联：而是绝对者自身的第二个循环，这绝对者已经生成精神，作为这样的精神，作为生育出来的总体性，作为精神，作为意识，进入那种痛苦之中，以致精神作为意识在自身这个已经生成者身上产生出那种自己的生成。—— 宗教的那种直观是普遍的宗教，而它只有作为科学才是这样。
不是一种穿过，不是把那条最初的道路在自身之内作为一种直观着的循环产生出来；而是科学把自己提高到信仰及其直观之上，它作为精神离开自己，又作为精神回到自己。
那种直观的教养，那种直观的科学发展就在于：它始终是精神，不失去精神，并且作为这种不失去自身的精神，它对自己成为一个他者，又重新找到自己。
知识把直观的每一个环节——这环节自为地是一个不可穿透的特定形态，它并不敞开自己的内在，而是产生出来、行动，并通过另一个行动者而消失——变成一个在自身之内的过程，或者说变成一种精神的自然。

en: Bad reflection is the fear of immersing oneself in the matter, [it wants] always to go beyond it and to return into itself.
The analyst, as Laplace says, surrenders himself to the calculus, and the task vanishes for him, i.e. the overview and the dependence of the individual moments of the calculation on the whole.

Not only is insight into the dependence of the individual on the whole alone the essential, [but] equally that every moment itself, independent of the whole, is the whole, and this is the immersion into the matter.
zh: 坏的反思是害怕深入事情本身，[它想要]总是超出事情并回到自身。
分析家，如拉普拉斯所说，把自己交给演算，于是任务对他消失了，也就是说，对整体的概观以及计算的各个别环节对整体的依赖消失了。
不仅对个别东西依赖整体的洞见才是本质性的东西，[而且]同样地，每个环节本身即使不依赖整体也是整体，而这就是深入事情本身。

en: Faust found the limits of humanity too narrow and struck against them with wild force in order to push them beyond actuality.
He found the noble mind oppressed and neglected, the fool and scoundrel raised to honours.
He wants to investigate the ground of moral evil, the relation of man to the eternal, whether there is one who guides the human race, and whence the contradictions plaguing it arise.
He wants to have the ground of things, the secret springs of the appearances of the physical and moral world, and to have graspably him who has ordered everything.
zh: 浮士德觉得人性的界限太窄，便以狂野的力量去撞击它，为的是把这些界限推移到现实性之外。
他发现高贵的头脑受到压制和冷落，傻瓜和恶棍却被抬举起来享受荣誉。
他要探究道德之恶的根据，人同永恒者的关系，是否有一个引导人类者存在，以及那些折磨人类的矛盾从何而来。
他要掌握事物的根据，物理世界和道德世界各种现象的隐秘发条，并且要清楚地掌握那个安排了一切者。

en: In vain!
He hurries onto the stage of life, where virtue and vice are entangled, good comes from evil, evil from good.
The spirit grows ever more confused.
He sees the chain of necessity wound around free creatures, gnashes his teeth that no one is master of his deeds, and cannot change it.
He must let everything go its eternal course, whereas that power which he does not see, which seems only to mock him, wraps itself in deep darkness, gloomy silence.
To the spirit of man everything is dark; he is a riddle to himself.
zh: 徒劳！
他匆匆登上生活的舞台，在那里德行与恶行纠缠在一起，善出自恶，恶出自善。
精神越来越混乱。
他看见必然性的锁链缠绕在自由的造物身上，为谁都不是自己行为的主人而咬牙切齿，却又无法改变这一点。
他必须让一切走自己永恒的路，而那种他看不见的、似乎只是在嘲弄他的力量，却把自己裹在深深的黑暗、阴沉的沉默之中。
对人的精神来说一切都是昏暗的，他自己对自己就是一个谜。

en: Theology grants what speculation refuses: what did I do to your God, I who only strove to fulfil the laws of humanity according to the guidance of the heart - to your God, who upon no sacrifice came to the aid of your wishes, stilled none of your sufferings, to whom the one tormented by you cries in vain?
Necessity is the name of the mighty, unknown power.
This is all that you grasp.
Submit and die.
zh: 神学给予思辨所拒绝给予的东西：我对你们的上帝做了什么，我只是努力按照心的指引去履行人类的法则——对你们的上帝，他不曾为任何献祭而帮助你们的愿望，不曾平息你们的任何痛苦，而你们所折磨的人向他徒然呼救？
必然性就是那种强大的、未知的力量的名字。
这就是你所能把握的全部。
屈服吧，去死吧。

en: Not the deity, but humanity itself, through misuse of its gifts, through false application of its capacities, through faint-heartedness and sloth, bears the guilt of everything.
The human being misuses what has been given him for his happiness: religion, government and science.

Most happy is he who, in quiet repose, far from the noisy activity of men, lives out his days without knowing how men are governed, and without inquiring why God lets things happen before our eyes as we see them happen daily.
But can the human being do that?
Does he determine his situation and his fate?
Is he not violently swept into the whirlpool of life?
The great Why returns.
zh: 不是神性，而是人类自己，由于滥用它的赠礼、由于错误地运用它的能力、由于怯懦和懒惰，承担着一切的罪责。
人滥用为了他的幸福而给予他的东西，宗教、政府和科学。
最幸福的是这样一个人，他在静静的安宁里，远离人们喧闹的活动，度过自己的日子，既不知道人们是怎样被统治的，也不去追问上帝为什么在我们眼前让事情发生，正如我们每天看见它们发生一样。
可是人能做到这一点吗？
他能决定自己的处境和命运吗？
他不是被强行卷进生活的漩涡里吗？
那个巨大的“为什么”又回来了。

en: The human being who no longer accuses God but acknowledges his dependence wants to know for what purpose he is there.
And if he can force no answer, he would still like to know why nature has stopped halfway with him and only lets him surmise where he demands certainty.
The human being is master of his fate and of his determination.
Through his activity he can further and disturb the fair course of the moral world, and the whole human race, from beggar to king, is master-builder of the moral world.

The human being develops only the striving laid into him, like every thing of the visible world, only with the difference that only he is made capable of punishment and reward by his free will and by his sense that comprehends evil and good. - I have conquered the inclination to evil.

The purity of my will it is, the feeling of having acted according to the laws of reason, the conviction that a being cannot pass away that has worked through the understanding, - these are what elevate me. - Restless, bold, often fruitless struggle of the noble man with the spectres generated by these gods: diremption of the heart and the understanding; the sublime dreams and the animal, corrupt ones; the pure and lofty sense, heroic deeds and crimes; prudence and madness; violence and sighing submission; the whole human society with its wonders and follies, horrors and excellences. - But - is that enthusiasm really more than the dream of a visionary?
Does cold understanding justify it?
Do we not, following it, chase after empty shadows and lose the essential being in doing so?
Yes, as the world now is, as its present relations are, can such a dream be realized at all?
zh: 那个不再控告上帝、却承认自己依赖上帝的人，想要知道他为了什么目的而存在。
而如果他逼不出任何回答，他还是想知道，为什么自然在他这里中途就停住了，只让他在他要求确定性的地方去猜测。
人是自己命运和自身规定的主人。
他能通过自己的作为促进和扰乱道德世界的美好进程，而整个人类，从乞丐到国王，都是道德世界的工匠。
人只是发展出放进他里面的那种努力，就像可见世界中的每一个事物一样，唯一的区别在于，只有他，才由自己的自由意志和那种以概念把握恶与善的意识，而变得能够承受刑罚和得到奖赏。——我已经战胜了向恶的倾向。

是我的意志的纯洁，是按照理性的法则行动过的感觉，是那种确信——一个通过知性起了作用的存在不可能消逝——是这些在提升我。——高贵者与这些神所生出的幽灵之间那不停息、勇敢、常常没有结果的斗争：心与知性的分裂；那些崇高的梦和那些兽性的、败坏的梦；纯洁而高尚的意识，英雄行为与罪行；明智与疯狂；暴力与叹息的屈服；整个人类社会连同它的种种奇迹与愚蠢、种种丑恶与优点。——可是——那种热情难道真的不止是一个狂热者的梦吗？
冷静的知性会为它辩护吗？
我们跟着它，难道不是在追逐空洞的影子，并且因此失去本质吗？
是啊，就世界现在这个样子、就它目前的关系来说，这样一个梦究竟能不能实现呢？

en: Spirit of nature: live in me, with me!
I am with you and cannot become clearer to you than I am!
Blossoming and withering, thriving and destroying hang together.
My friendship hides from you the close concatenation.
I have given my dear children deception as a companion along the way.
My reward is your happiness.
The source of it streams with a rich flow in your heart.
Seek it only there!
Flee the delusion of those who seek it outside me!
zh: 自然的精神：在我之中活着，与我一同活着！
我与你们同在，我没法对你们变得比我现在的样子更清楚！
开花与凋谢、繁盛与毁坏，彼此连在一起。
我的友谊向你们遮住了这种切近的连结。
我把欺瞒当作同伴，交给我亲爱的孩子们一同带上了路。
我的报酬就是你们的幸福。
它的源头以丰沛的河流涌流在你们心中。
就在那里寻找它吧！
要躲开那些在我之外寻找它的人的妄想！

en: Everyone wants and believes himself to be better than this world of his.
Whoever is better only expresses this world of his better than others do.
zh: 每个人都想要、并且自以为比他自己这个世界更好。
谁更好，也只是比其他人更好地表达出他自己这个世界。

en: The ordinary royal road in philosophy is to read the prefaces and reviews in order to get an approximate representation of the matter.
zh: 哲学里通常的那条王道，就是读序言和书评，好对事情得到一个大概的表象。

en: The last royal road in studying is thinking for oneself.
zh: 研究时最后一条王道，就是自己思考。

en: Those who say so much against philosophical systems overlook, in the case of a particular system, the circumstance that it is a philosophy; [the] main circumstance, just as that an oak is a tree.
zh: 那些对哲学体系说了那么多反对话的人，在某个特定的体系那里忽略了这样一个情况，即它是一种哲学；[这个]主要情况，正如一棵橡树是一棵树一样。

en: Kiesewetter has found a very great inclination among the deaf and dumb to speak in rhymes, and what seems almost unbelievable: their rhymes were based not on orthography but on sound.
zh: 基泽韦特（Kiesewetter）发现聋哑人有一种极大的倾向，就是用韵说话，而且，这一点几乎令人难以置信：他们的韵不是建立在正字法上，而是建立在声音上。

en: To speak in one's own language is one of the highest moments of culture.
A people belongs to itself.
The foreignness, down to the Latin letters, out!
zh: 用自己的语言说话，是最高的教养环节之一。
一个民族属于自己。
把这种异己性赶出去，直到拉丁字母也不例外！

en: Someone steps forward and delivers something mediocre.
Everyone greets him as one of their equals and cherishes and fosters him: you are one of us, you don't really mean it seriously, etc.
zh: 有一个人站出来，交出某种平庸的东西。
所有人都把他当作自己人一样来欢迎，疼爱他、照料他：你是我们的人，你并不当真，等等。

en: In the case of philosophy the public is concerned with religion, the lost one; not with science; with that only afterwards.
The human being wants to learn how he stands, wants satisfaction for himself, the interest of humanity of this time.
zh: 在哲学上，公众所关心的是宗教，那失去了的宗教；不是科学；科学要到后来才谈得上。
人想要知道自己处境如何，想要为自己得到满足，想要这个时代的人类的利益。

en: "Fine sciences" is no longer said, but still: think of a house with two trunks beside it, etc., instead of: represent to yourself.
zh: “美的科学”已经不再有人说了，但还有人说：你设想一座旁边立着两根树干的房子等等，而不是说：你把它表象出来。

en: It is no longer so much a matter of thoughts.
We have enough of them, good and bad, beautiful and bold.
But of concepts.

But since the former are to be made valid immediately through themselves, whereas as concepts they are to be made comprehensible, the form of writing thereby receives a change, an appearance perhaps demanding painful exertion, as with Plato, Aristotle.
zh: 如今所关乎的已经不太是思想了。
我们有足够多的思想，好的和坏的，美的和大胆的。
而是关乎概念。
但既然那些思想是要通过自身直接生效的，而作为概念却应当被弄得能被概念把握，于是写作方式的形式就由此得到一种改变，一种也许要求令人难受的努力的外观，正如在柏拉图、亚里士多德那里那样。

en: The effect on the public is an absolute standard, over which the subject may well go mad.
It has done everything; but precisely the unconscious instinct stands opposed to its insight.
zh: 在公众身上产生的效果是一个绝对的标准，主体为此发疯也不奇怪。
它什么都做了；但恰恰是无意识的本能与它的洞见相对立。

en: On morality: its highest thing, to bury the guilt and the sufferings of this heart in the heart itself, to make the heart into the grave of the heart.
zh: 论道德：道德的最高者，就是把这颗心的罪责和痛苦埋葬在它自身里，把心变成心的坟墓。

en: With the miracles of the New Testament, what matters is not the content of the miracle, but that it is a miracle.
What does it matter - the healing of a withered hand, the withering of a fig tree, or the drunkenness of the wedding guests!
zh: 在《新约》的种种奇迹那里，要紧的不是奇迹的内容，而是它是一个奇迹。
治好一只枯干的手，使一棵无花果树枯干，或者让婚礼的客人喝醉，又有什么关系！

en: A patched stocking is better than a torn one; not so self-consciousness.
zh: 一只补过的袜子比一只破袜子好；自我意识却不是这样。

en: To study means to come to regard as true what others have thought.
But if one thinks to be done with it at once, as with something false, one does not know the things.
zh: 研究就意味着，学会把别人所想过的东西看作真的。
但如果人一开始就想把它当作虚假的东西一下子了结掉，那他就还不认识这些事物。

en: Since religion is lost, one demands of philosophy that it devote itself to edifying and stand in for the pastor.
zh: 宗教既然已经失去，人们就要求哲学去负责启迪人心，代替牧师。

en: The dividing wall between the terminology of philosophy and that of ordinary consciousness is still to be broken through; the reluctance to think what is familiar.
It is to rest quietly at that, philosophy is not to be taken in earnest; but this philosophy does, when it turns to what is common and current.
zh: 哲学的术语与普通意识之间的隔墙还有待打破；那种不愿去思考已知东西的抗拒。
事情该就此安安静静地作罢，不该对哲学认真起来；但哲学一旦转向那些通行习见的东西，它就是这样做的。

en: Philosophy is not granted the good fortune to have a proposition and to be able to say: that is, or is nothing.
zh: 哲学没有那样的福气，能拥有一个命题，还能说：它是，或者什么也不是。

en: Kant is cited with admiration for teaching philosophizing, not philosophy; as if someone taught carpentry but not how to make a table, chair, door, cupboard, etc.
zh: 人们怀着钦佩引用康德的话，说他教的是哲学思考，不是哲学；就好像有人教木工手艺，却不教做桌子、椅子、门、柜子等等。

en: 256) Ideas of the philosophy of nature, i.e. fantastic and unreasonable.
The excitation through philosophy is only an irritation that comes to no substantiality.
zh: 256) 自然哲学的观念，也就是说，幻想的、非理性的。
由哲学引起的激动只是一种刺激，达不到任何实体性。

en: The perfect is indeed everywhere only one, but especially in art the great thing: not to want to make the statue coloured; not to unite the lyrical element of the chorus with the dramatic element of the persons; - so too not to unite philosophizing with poetizing, - in general to resolve upon the necessary separation and to maintain it strictly.
zh: 完美的东西诚然到处都只是一个，但在艺术中尤其是那伟大的东西：不想把雕像做成彩色的；不把合唱队的抒情成分与剧中人物的戏剧成分合在一起；——同样也不把哲学思考与作诗合在一起，——总之，下决心去作那必要的分离，并严格地保持它。

en: One grows anxious and afraid.

When they hear of a thing, a matter or stuff - it is to be nothing but idea. - Just as nowadays no one with Homer may compare Ajax to a donkey, so learning is a word that is no longer heard in good society.
zh: 人不由得害怕、心慌。
他们一听到一个东西、一种物质或材料——它应该纯然是观念。——正如现在没有人能像荷马那样把埃阿斯比作一头驴，学习也是一个词，在上流圈子里再也听不到了。

en: Only after the history of consciousness does one know, through the concept, what one has in these abstractions: Fichte's merit.
zh: 只有在意识的历史之后，人才通过概念知道，人在这些抽象那里拥有什么：费希特的功劳。

en: Plato studied with many philosophers, took long, hard pains, made journeys, was probably no productive genius, nor a poetic one, but a slow head.
God gives it to the genius in sleep.
What he gives them in sleep, however, are for that reason only dreams.
zh: 柏拉图在许多哲学家那里学习过，长时间下苦功，外出旅行，大概不是什么有创造力的天才，也不是作诗的天才，而是一个迟钝的头脑。
上帝在睡梦里把它赐给天才。
但他在睡梦里给他们的东西，因此也只是些梦。

en: Oriental: water: father of life, father of the clouds; honey: father of victory; sugar: f. of healing; meat: f. of abundance; wine: f. of easy digestion; bread: f. of the graces, f. of mankind; bed: f. of the desires; zither: f. of play; good companion: f. of perfection; cheese: f. of the traveller - etc., a superficial designation which, because it is such a general description, must again be known according to its meaning, like a sign, and is not clear for itself.
zh: 东方的：水：生命之父、云之父；蜂蜜：胜利之父；糖：治疗之父；肉：丰足之父；酒：容易消化之父；面包：恩典之父、人类之父；床铺：欲望之父；齐特琴：游戏之父；好同伴：完美之父；奶酪：旅行者之父——等等，这是一种肤浅的称呼，它正因为是这样普遍的描述，就又必须像符号一样按其含义为人所知，而不是凭自身就清楚的。

en: Reviewers are gravediggers.
But even if they bury what is living, it still preserves itself.
They themselves have to learn.
To judge, to characterize means to kill, to present the individual, not the matter, as if the former were the living, not the true.
Judges of the secret court, Freemasons are no further than the rest of the public, are themselves backward.
When the mystery is made manifest, they have to do only with what is merely meant.
zh: 写书评的人是掘墓人。
但即使他们埋葬的是活的东西，它还是保存了下来。
他们自己还得学习。
判断、刻画特征就意味着杀死，就是描述个体，而不是描述事情，仿佛那个体才是活的东西，而不是真的东西。
秘密法庭的法官、共济会员并不比其余公众走得更远，他们自己还落在后面。
一旦秘密被公开出来，他们打交道的就只是被意谓的东西。

en: The time seems unfavourable to philosophy, because it seems to be a matter of so much trouble that only the thought of the supersensible should come about, the first crude beginning; but it is to be exhibited in the most familiar thing, e.g. fruit; not a sense for religion in general.
zh: 时代对哲学显得不利，因为看来要用那么多力气去做的，只是让对超感性东西的思想得以成立，即那最初粗糙的开端；但它应当在最熟知的东西上、例如水果上，被指出来；而不是一般地对宗教的感受。

en: In the Cid it says:
zh: 《熙德》里这样说：

en: But which vanquished man does not complain of injustice.
zh: 可是，哪个被战胜的人不抱怨不公呢。

en: Philosophy governs the representations, and these govern the world.
Through consciousness spirit reaches into the dominion of the world.
This is its infinite tool; beyond that, bayonets, cannons, bodies.
But their banner, and the soul of their commander, is spirit.
Not bayonets, not money, not individual tricks and dodges are what rules.
This too must be so, as the clock has wheels, but its soul is time and the spirit that subjects matter to its law.
An Iliad is not thrown together, nor likewise a great work out of bayonets and cannons, but the composer is spirit.
zh: 哲学支配着表象，而这些表象支配着世界。
精神通过意识介入世界的统治。
这是它无限的工具，再往外则是刺刀、大炮、肉体。
但它们的旗帜和它们统帅的灵魂，是精神。
不是刺刀，不是金钱，不是个别的手腕和花招在起支配作用。
这也必定如此，就像钟有齿轮，但它的灵魂是时间，是那个使物质服从自己法则的精神。
一部《伊利亚特》不是拼凑起来的，一部由刺刀和大炮做成的大作品也不是，相反，组合者是精神。

en: Unity and difference sounds poor and meagre, e.g. against the splendour of the sun, against East and West, that every thing has its East and West in itself.
But to the poor the gospel is preached, and they shall see God.
zh: 统一和区别听起来贫乏、寒碜，比如比起太阳的壮丽，比起东方和西方，即每个事物在自身中都有自己的东方和西方。
但福音是传给穷人的，而他们将看见上帝。

en: Philosophy of nature.

It will be a good while yet before things there go on entirely without humbug. - Admission of this, or brazen assertion and insistence to the contrary. - The absolute: at night all cows are black. - Absolute cognition [is] the great broom that sweeps everything away, qui fait la maison nette.
zh: 自然哲学。
还要过相当长的时间，那里才会完全没有糊弄。——对此的承认，或者厚着脸皮的断言并坚持相反的说法。——绝对者：夜里所有的牛都是黑的。——绝对认识就是那把大扫帚，把一切都扫掉，qui fait la maison nette。

en: Unterwalden: shepherd life.
No progress of spiritual culture.
Nourishment of the inclination to indolence.
The teachers of religion dependent on the people, which elects them and has their upkeep in its power.
This dependence makes them intriguing.
They flatter the uneducated crowd, thrust themselves into family secrets, keep up parties and acquire a widespread dominion over minds in rural communities.

They were not allowed to make any use of this dominion to recommend to ignorant and narrow-minded people anything that deviates from the customary; no useful school institutions, only crudeness, savagery.

It is the interest of the politics of the wealthier families, in order to preserve their influence and offices, to let that savagery be. - The freedom of the uneducated mass becomes poverty, melancholy.
The churches not empty of praying men, the streets not of pilgrims, the graves not of kneelers.
But along with this a worsening of morals, gloating over the loss of the envied rich and slander, faithlessness and ingratitude.
Bad husbandry and gluttony with all poverty; petty, beggarly self-interest.
With lack of agriculture, with decay of the forests, with absence of industry, yet an increase of luxury.
zh: 翁特瓦尔登：牧人生活。
精神教养没有进步。
懒惰倾向的养料。
宗教教师依赖于民众，民众选举他们，而他们的生计也掌握在民众手里。
这种依赖使他们变得爱搞阴谋。
他们讨好未受教养的大众，钻进家庭秘密里，维持派系，并在乡村村社中赢得对人心的一种广泛统治。
他们不许利用这种统治去向无知而狭隘的人推荐任何偏离习惯的东西；没有有益的学校机构，只有粗野、野蛮化。
较富裕家族的政治利益在于，为了保住自己的影响和官职，让那种野蛮化继续下去。——未受教养群众的自由变成贫困、忧郁。
教堂里不缺祈祷的人，街上不缺朝圣的人，坟前不缺跪着的人。
但与此同时风气变坏，对被人嫉妒的富人遭受损失幸灾乐祸，还有诽谤、不忠和忘恩负义。
尽管一贫如洗，还是经营不善、大吃大喝；还有卑琐的、乞丐似的自私自利。
在农业缺乏、森林衰败、工艺勤勉缺失的情况下，奢华却仍在增长。

en: Cid:
zh: Cid:

en: The secret is the power of women over our men's hearts.
The secret sits deep hidden in them, inscrutable, I believe, even to God the Lord himself.
When on that great day, which one day will seek out all faults, God sifts the hearts of women, he finds them either all guilty or all equally innocent: so interwoven is their heart.
zh: 这秘密就是女人对我们男人心的威力。
这秘密深藏在她们心里，我想，连主上帝自己也探究不出。
到了那大日子，有朝一日要追究一切过失，上帝来查验女人的心时，他找出来的是要么全都有罪，要么全都一样无罪：她们的心就这样缠在一起。

en: In Lucerne round hats over 18 inches in diameter have been forbidden, as a luxury that corrupts the land!
zh: 在卢塞恩（Luzern），直径超过 18 英寸的圆帽子已经作为败坏地方的奢侈被禁止了！

en: In philosophizing there is nothing to picture.
Here and there an image.
That is what people hold on to.
Tabula rasa from Aristotle, incidentally, used out of need.
That much everyone knows about Aristotle.
It does not express the essential thing in his concept of the soul.
zh: 在哲学思考里，没有什么可供表象。
这里那里一幅图像。
人们就抓住这些。
亚里士多德的白板，偶然地被拿来应急。
关于亚里士多德，人人所知不过如此。
这并没有道出他灵魂概念里本质性的东西。

en: Luden's History of Hugo Grotius, 231: at that time the rumour was spread that the king (Gustav Adolf after the battle of Lützen) was still alive; he had spread the report of his death for good reasons.
These homines acuti, says Grotius, nos velut crassos, qui mortuum mortuum credimus, irrident. Hoc est Germaniae acumen
.257) - Just so, when the philosopher judges that a state or the like is dead, the reply is, it is still alive, the imperial diet and so on. Hoc est Germaniae acumen!
zh: 卢登的《格劳秀斯史》，231：当时流传着一个谣言，说国王（吕岑之战后的古斯塔夫·阿道夫）还活着；他出于充分的理由散布了自己死掉的消息。
这些 homines acuti，格劳秀斯说，nos velut crassos, qui mortuum mortuum credimus, irrident。Hoc est Germaniae acumen
.257）——同样，当哲学家判定一个国家之类已经死了，人们就说，它明明还活着，帝国议会等等。Hoc est Germaniae acumen！

en: The divinity is worshipped in the work of art, in the bad one as in the excellent one.
The awe of the divinity, the annihilation of the individual, pervades the assembly.
But soon it breathes again, looks about among living beings, wakes to the feeling of life.
They recognize themselves as life, sound it out to one another, clasp hands, feel themselves and pass over into movement, into dance.
The rejoicing must turn into harmony, into manifoldness of images and thoughts.
Measure through rhythm becomes the holding back of the subjective, of the arbitrary.
The individuals become members of the objective unity.
Like Kybele, the great mother of the gods, she herself beats the drums; otherwise she works in quiet unconscious force.
Thus the divinity enjoys itself, and man has identified himself with it.
This enjoyment is skipped over in the eating of the divinity, but it expresses deeply the infinite pain, the complete shattering of what is innermost.
God sacrifices himself, gives himself over to annihilation.
God himself is dead; the highest despair of utter forsakenness by God.
zh: 神性在艺术作品里受到敬拜，在坏的作品里和在出色的作品里都一样。
对神性的敬畏，个体的消亡，穿透了整个聚会的人群。
但它很快就喘过气来，环顾四周的活物，醒过来感受生命。
他们认出自己是生命，彼此把它唱和出来，拉起手，感觉到自己，进而转入运动，转入舞蹈。
欢呼必须变成和谐，变成图像和想法的杂多。
由节拍而来的尺度，变成对主观的东西、对任意的东西的约束。
个体成了客观统一的环节。
她像库柏勒（Kybele），诸神的大母，自己敲起鼓来，否则她就在静默的无意识力量中起作用。
神性就这样享受自己，而人已经把自己与它等同起来。
在吃神的时候，这种享受被跳过去了，但它深深地表达了无限的痛苦，表达了最内在的东西的彻底破碎。
神牺牲自己，把自己交出去受消亡。
神自己死了；这是被神完全遗弃的最高绝望。

en: The joy in the St John's fire only needed to be organized.
On all the mountains a quantity of fires are lit.
It is the joy in the first fire, and what is the joy in such a living element other than something religious?
For it is the joy in it itself as an element.
This joy must honour itself, order itself with consciousness, make itself lawful.
This joy only needs to be taken in earnest, and so it is a divine service.
But it is not taken so.

Man, in the religion of pain, despises his joy, rejects the consciousness of it. - With the Greeks it is otherwise, for they made even eating a divine service, i.e. enjoyed it with consciousness and will.
With us, boredom is at home.
A company is ashamed of eating.
There are no more serious people than the Greeks, and none more cheerful.
zh: 对约翰节篝火的欢乐，只需要组织起来就行了。
所有的山上都会点起一堆一堆的火。
这是对最初的火的那种欢乐，而对这样一个活生生的元素的欢乐，除了是宗教性的东西，还能是什么？
因为这是对火本身作为一个元素的欢乐。
这种欢乐必须自己敬重自己，带着意识把自己安排有序，使自己合乎法则。
这种欢乐只需要被当作严肃的事情，那它就是一场礼拜。
但它并没有被这样对待。
在痛苦的宗教里，人蔑视自己的欢乐，抛弃对欢乐的意识。——希腊人则不同，他们连吃饭也做成一场礼拜，也就是说，带着意识和意志去享用。
在我们这里，无聊安了家。
同席的人会为吃饭感到羞耻。
再也没有比希腊人更认真的人，也没有比他们更快活的人。

en: Formerly the lower class of the people cast out individual family members as the scapegoat, on whom lies the burden of deprivation, of penance and of self-estrangement, to the point of madness, while it itself came off free and bought reconciliation for itself through these sacrifices.
But now it has taken the penance itself upon itself.
zh: 从前，低下的民众阶层把个别的家庭成员赶出去当替罪羊，匮乏、忏悔苦行和自我异化的重担压在他们身上，直到发疯，而它自己反倒脱身无事，靠这些献祭为自己买来了和解。
可现在，它把悔改本身担到了自己身上。

en: Rather let ten millions be taken from one by force, let oneself be spat in the face, be trampled underfoot, be beaten, than voluntarily give a million, voluntarily expose oneself to a wound while dealing out wounds: that is the sense of the German nation.

With a tenth of the expenditure in money and goods in kind, with a thousandth of the sufferings, with the saving of the mountain of shame that the past war has cost the Germans, they could, through 9/10 of what was lost, have averted 999/1000 of the sufferings and, instead of shame, have won honour.
But the Germans want [rather] to have the satisfaction of remaining neutral, i.e. to let themselves be fleeced by both sides, than to attach themselves to one side.
They have the satisfaction of having nevertheless remained for themselves.
They are the Quaker nation of Europe.
They let everything be taken from them, their coat too, and out of good nature, in order not to get an angry face, they even give the waistcoat.
When they get a slap in the face from one side, from one of the warring powers, they put themselves in the position of having to get one from the other too.
As Tertullian describes the Christians.
zh: 宁可让人用暴力拿走一千万，让人往自己脸上吐唾沫、用脚踩自己、揍自己，也不愿自愿交出一百万，自愿在分发创伤的同时让自己也暴露在一处创伤面前：这就是德意志民族的本性。
用十分之一的金钱和实物花费，用千分之一的苦难，省下那场过去的战争让德意志人付出的堆积如山的耻辱，他们本可以用失去的东西的 9/10 免去 999/1000 的苦难，并且换来荣誉而不是耻辱。
可是德意志人[宁可]要得到保持中立的那份满意，也就是说，让双方都来把自己榨干，也不愿依附于其中一方。
他们得到的满足是：毕竟还是留在了自己这一边。
他们是欧洲的贵格会民族。
他们由着别人拿走自己的一切，连外衣也拿走，而且出于好心，为了不看到一张难看的脸色，他们连背心也一并给出去。
要是他们从一方、从交战列强中的一方挨了一记耳光，他们就摆好架势，让自己也得从另一方挨上一记。
就像德尔图良描述基督徒那样。

en: By the "how" of a thing one means its kind. Four wooden legs, a board over them, is the "how" of a chair, i.e. precisely the chair itself.
zh: 说到一件事物的“如何”，人们指的是它的种类。四条木腿，上面搁一块板，这就是椅子的“如何”，也就是说，正是椅子本身。

en: The necessity of laws against usury.
Because the individual does not know the occasions and the individuals with whom money is to be had, this appears rarer than it is.
The state, by contrast, is to have this knowledge of the scarcity or quantity of money.
Its rate of interest supplies the consequence from which that embarrassment would spring, namely the opinion of greater scarcity and thereby the emergence of higher interest.
Further, how on corn prices every rumour of war and peace, hailstorms etc.
has an influence, so the same fluctuation would set in with money.

It is this inconstancy that raises the price, for the hope of selling higher or at least not lower is stronger than the fear of the opposite, and the former brings about holding back more strongly than the latter does selling off.
Hence rates on bread, meat etc. necessary.
zh: 反高利贷的法律的必然性。
因为单个的人不知道有哪些机会、哪些人手里有钱，所以这种情况看起来比实际上更少见。
相反，国家则应当具备这种知识：知道货币是稀少还是充裕。
它的利息价率补上了那个后果，也就是以为货币更稀少、并因此生出更高利息的看法，而那种窘迫本来会从这一后果中产生。
再者，正如战争与和平的每一条传言、冰雹天气等等对谷物价格，
有影响一样，货币这边也会出现同样的波动。
正是这种不稳定抬高了价格，因为想卖得更高、至少不卖得更低的这种希望，比相反的恐惧更强，而前者对捂货不卖的推动，也比后者对抛售的推动更强。
所以，对面包、肉等等的价率是必要的。

en: Κουϱιδίη ἄλοχος - that this woman should not be exhausted by frequent childbeds - slave women. - The inequality in general of the duration of desire and the man's capacity as against the charms, fertility and health of the woman is, given the holiness of marriage among the Europeans, a disproportion that always keeps up a mute struggle, inward discord and the evil of debauchery among a people.258)
zh: Κουϱιδίη ἄλοχος——这女人不会因频繁坐月子而被耗尽——女奴。——欲望的持续时间与男人的能力相对于女人的魅力、生育力和健康而言的总体不平等，在欧洲人这里，鉴于婚姻的神圣性，是一种不相称，它总是在一个民族中间维持着一场无声的斗争、内心的争执和放纵的恶习。258）

en: There is no country like Germany, where every notion is at once made into something general, trained up into the idol of the day, and the setting-up of the same is driven to charlatanry, so that it is just as quickly forgotten and the fruit is lost that it would bear if it had been confined within its limit.

Thereby it would be recognized in its measure and valued and used as much as belongs to it, whereas in the other way, with its undue inflation, it at the same time shrinks up entirely and, as said, is forgotten.
zh: 没有哪个国家像德意志这样，在那里，每一个念头都立刻被弄成某种普遍的东西，被培养成当日的偶像，而把同一个念头摆出来又被推到江湖骗术的地步，结果它也同样很快被忘掉，它若被限制在自己的界限之内本来会结出的果实也就丢失了。
这样一来，它就会在它的尺度内被认识，并且得到它应得的那份重视和使用，而[与此相反]，以另一种方式，随着它那不合分寸的膨胀，它同时也整个儿缩塌下去，并且如前面所说，被忘掉。

en: The South Germans honestly reprinted it.
The North Germans copy themselves out and repeat the same thing; compendia, a chapter earlier or later; even elegant newspapers.
zh: 南德意志人老老实实地翻印了。
北德意志人则从别人那里抄出来，重复同样的东西；各种纲要，早一章或晚一章；连那些优雅的报纸也一样。

en: I remember very well how long I roamed about in the sciences, honestly thinking that what of it was manifest was not yet all.

From the phrases used to conduct the matter I concluded that the essence still lurked in the background and that everyone knew far more than they said, namely the spirit and the grounds for advancing such a thing.

After I had long searched in vain for where this was to be found, that of which people always spoke or did as if it were the universally known and the doings of the ordinary thus the right thing, and could not find its justification, I found that in fact there was no more to it than I well understood, and beyond that only this: the tone of confidence, arbitrariness and presumption.
zh: 我很清楚地记得，我在各门科学里游荡了多久，老老实实地以为，其中已经明白可见的东西并不是全部。
从人们用来处理事情的种种说法里，我推断出，本质还藏在幕后，而人人所知道的都远远多于他们所说的，即那种精神，以及把这类东西推向前进的理由。
我长久徒劳地寻找：人们总是谈论或做着的这东西，仿佛它就是大家已知的东西、而寻常人的作为因此就是对的，究竟在哪里可以找到；也找不到对它的正当理由；此后我发现，事实上它并不比我很好地理解到的更多，除此之外就只有这一点：那种确信的语气、任意和狂妄。

en: A friend of genuine natural science proposes that the amply well-known Herr Dr. Gall259), who to the greatest astonishment has already completed a course, be asked to hold another one, since it is clear from his lecture that he is inexhaustible and will still know how to tell us new stories.
For the time being he has already declared himself not disinclined to this and promised to bring his skull-emptiness even more to light through new arrangements.
For he will:
zh: 一位真正的自然研究之友提议，请那位已经足够有名的加尔博士先生259)——令人大为惊奇的是，他已经讲完了一轮课程——再讲一轮，因为从他的讲演可以看出，他是取之不尽的，还会一直给我们讲出新的故事来。
目前他已经表示对此并非不乐意，并且答应，要通过新的安排，把他的颅骨空学更多地摆到明处。
也就是说，他将会：

en: 1. unfold his flat skin to present the brain; on a little apron for the chapeaux, for the ladies on a pair of trousers;
zh: 1. 为展示大脑，把他那层扁平的皮展开；在一只为礼帽准备的小围裙上，为女士们则在一条裤子上；

en: 2. show the origin of the nerves from the tailbone;
zh: 2. 显示神经从尾骨的发源；

en: 3. point out a great number of new senses, in ladies besides the dancing sense also the sewing and cooking sense, in boorish clods the flail sense, but in others the charlatan sense, all without thinking;
zh: 3. 指出一大批新的感官，在女士身上除了舞蹈感还有缝纫感和烹饪感，在乡巴佬身上是连枷感，在另一些人身上则是江湖骗子感，所有这些都不用思考；

en: 4. call in the comb-woman from the orphanage, Barbara Sprützbein, who with her fluent manipulation of skulls and her experience will support Herr Dr. Gall.
zh: 4. 把孤儿院里的梳头妇 Barbara Sprützbein 请来，她会用她熟练地摆弄头骨的手法和她的经验来支持加尔博士先生。

en: One enlightens the age, another feels it up in sonnets, educates it up, reflects, gazes it up, prays it up.

The age is for everyone the truncus ficulnus, out of whose whole each wants to fabricate a Mercury; but the devil carries the truncus away from under his hands, or, to pass over into another simile, the Mont Blanc granite, and leaves him only a little splinter or grain, so that, when one now looks at his finished work by the light, he has brought out a damn small little Mercury and cannot rail enough about the wickedness of the time and of the devil, who has left him only such crumbs, so that now a multitude of little ages run about, all portraying it differently: Salzmannian, Campean, cowpox little ages; - to clarify it, that it become pure clear ether, out of which the star-shapes freely spring forth in the middle in eternal solar beauty.
zh: 一个把时代启蒙，另一个则用十四行诗把它感受上去、把它教育上去、反思它、把它仰望上去、把它祈祷上去。

时代对每个人来说都是那 truncus ficulnus，每个人都想从它的整体中造出一个墨丘利；但魔鬼却在他手底下把那 truncus，或者换个比喻说，把勃朗峰花岗岩拿走了，只给他留下一小块碎片或一粒细屑，于是，当人如今把自己的成品拿到光下细看时，他弄出来的是一个该死的小小墨丘利，于是他对时代和魔鬼的恶劣怎么也骂不够——魔鬼只给他留下了这样一些面包屑，结果现在有一大群小时代跑来跑去，它们描绘得各不相同：萨尔茨曼式的、坎佩式的、牛痘小时代；——把它澄清，使它成为纯净清澈的以太，星辰形态从其中自由地、在永恒的太阳之美中从中间跳出来。
